extracted.intended_audience: researchers, clinicians, journal editors, and readers interested in research integrity and publication ethics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and de facto standards about handling, processing, and verifying clinical images in medical case reports and journal submissions, with emphasis on disclosure, authenticity, and editorial verification. Focused on use of AI/tools to alter images, scale accuracy, and appropriate editorial remedies (e.g., retraction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to journal policies on image manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must follow the Journal's policies on image manipulation; failure to do so can lead to retraction. (Page quotes the retraction notice: “We were unaware of Journal policies on image manipulation and had altered our submission by using an artificial intelligence (AI) tool to move the ruler to the top of the image.”)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not alter submissions in ways that violate the journal's image policies. If any image processing is performed, it must be consistent with the journal's rules and be disclosed. Noncompliance may prompt retraction of the item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use AI to add or superimpose elements into clinical images
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit prohibition (de facto) against using AI tools to superimpose items (e.g., the authors used AI to move the ruler).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements such as scale bars, rulers, or other objects should not be AI-superimposed into clinical photographs. Using AI to insert or move such elements undermines authenticity and is treated as improper image manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose any image processing steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must disclose any image adjustments or processing. (Authors apologized: “We apologize for not disclosing this image processing step.”)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even minor adjustments (cropping, rotating, contrast) should be declared in the submission or figure caption per journal policy. Failure to disclose is an ethical breach and can trigger corrective actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor readability/visibility adjustments permissible only if they do not change clinical information
rubrics_metrics.description: Small edits intended to improve readability (e.g., straightening a tilted ruler) are defensible only when they do not alter clinical findings: “We only slightly adjusted the angle and position of the ruler to make the image neater and more readable, without changing any clinical information in the picture.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If making minor cosmetic edits, document them and ensure they do not modify anatomical structures, diagnostic features, or measurement scales. Even purportedly minor edits must be disclosed and verifiable with originals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve and verify scale accuracy and integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Scale markers/measurement tools in images must be accurate and not tampered with. PubPeer commenter noted anomalous numbering on the measuring tape (irregular counting around 30–40), which signaled manipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure scale bars and rulers are correct and unaltered. Any distortion, re-labeling, or repositioning that affects measurement interpretation is unacceptable. Reviewers and editors should scrutinize scales for anomalies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide original/raw images and supporting records upon request
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must be able to supply raw images and medical records for editorial verification; the authors “have sent their raw images to NEJM.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain original, unprocessed image files and associated metadata; submit them if editors request verification. Lack of originals undermines credibility and may lead to retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction is an appropriate remedy for undisclosed or improper image manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal retracted the case report after authors acknowledged using AI to alter the photo, demonstrating that undisclosed manipulation can lead to retraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals may issue corrections, expressions of concern, or retractions depending on severity; undisclosed alterations that affect trustworthiness typically justify retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial and peer-review scrutiny of images is required
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit expectation that editors and reviewers should detect problematic images (comments: “What were the Reviewers doing here?”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and editors should closely inspect submitted figures for anomalies (odd numbering, improbable features, signs of digital alteration) and request originals when in doubt. Image-checking protocols are part of quality control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid using dramatic or misleading imagery that could attract unwarranted media attention
rubrics_metrics.description: Dramatic visuals can draw media attention and increase the impact of any subsequent misconduct: “The dramatic visual drew attention in the media.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that images are accurate and not exaggerated for effect. Misleading or sensational images increase ethical risk and harm public trust if later found to be manipulated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain authenticity and traceability of data and image content
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep data authentic and traceable; authors claimed they did not fix the ruler numbering with AI “in order to keep all data authentic and traceable.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve provenance information (timestamps, metadata), avoid post-hoc edits that obscure origin, and be able to demonstrate how an image was acquired and processed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond transparently to post-publication scrutiny and concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors engaged with commenters (e.g., response to PubPeer) and supplied explanations and raw data to the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When concerns are raised publicly or by readers, authors should promptly cooperate with editors, provide originals, and clearly explain any processing; lack of cooperation escalates editorial responses.
